items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: He say, 'You know why? Because they're going to be talking about Ray Brown. They're going to be talking about Ron Carter.'

ctx.x: Yes, but you see once again you have to take under

consideration, there was such a shortage of bass players. You see what I'm saying. They wouldn't have chose me over Ray Brown, if Ray Brown was there. They wouldn't have chose me over Ron Carter or over someone, but just...they weren't there. That doesn't mean I was bad; my playing was bad, that don't mean I played bad, but it wasn't great either. But at least it was honest.

Then, I don't mean to underestimate or belittle myself in any way. I'm not apologizing, because I can honestly say after, say, the second year, I played good. Because I knew, I heard. I could hear for myself. I hear other people play and I know how to comment on them, my judgment on what I thought was good for somebody else.
